entities.name: CSFV
observations: Classical swine fever virus infection increased intracellular ROS in swine umbilical vein endothelial cells over 24–72 hours, measured by DHE fluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry.
Infected SUVECs showed increased thioredoxin, PRDX6, HO-1, and COX-2, decreased PPAR-γ, and antioxidant-sensitive viral replication.

entities.name: SUVECs
observations: CSFV infection directly induces ROS and compensatory redox-response changes in swine umbilical vein endothelial cells.

entities.name: CSFV NS5A
observations: Stable expression of CSFV NS5A in SUVEC lines increased ROS, increased thioredoxin and PRDX6 transcriptional activity, decreased HO-1, increased COX-2, and decreased PPAR-γ.
NS5A findings support a viral contribution to endothelial redox dysregulation but do not substitute for whole-virus infection evidence.

entities.name: CSFV SUVEC oxidative stress
observations: Direct infection studies support that CSFV induces oxidative stress in SUVECs, based primarily on increased intracellular ROS and coordinated antioxidant/inflammatory redox responses.
CSFV infection of primary PUVECs also altered redox-associated proteins including PRDX6, but retrieved evidence did not report direct ROS or biochemical oxidative-damage measurements.
